text.p: Here are the highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croatia is included in the network of European transport routes in the European transport conference in Helsinki: Two branches of the fifth route -- one connecting Budapest with Ploce via Sarajevo and the other with Rijeka via Zagreb -- cross through Croatia; and so is a good chunk of the tenth route -- Salzburg-Salonika via Zagreb and Belgrade.

- Croatian government will demand from the United Nations Administration in Eastern Slavonia to secure the harvest in the region. The request to be filed because of repeated Serb blackmail and danger from illegal export of wheat to Yugoslavia.

- The House of Counties, the upper house of the Croatian parliament, continued on Wednesday its 20th session, discussing law on sports. One of the proposals is for mass sport activities to be financed from the profit of lotteries.

- A Vjesnik editorial defends from criticism the recently proposed amendment to the constitution referring to the presidential oath which from now should end with words "So help me God". The editorial argues in support, quoting the examples of the U.S. and German presidential oaths, which include the same words.

- Lawyers of General Tihomir Blaskic, Bosnian Croat military commander tried in The Hague by the U.N. criminal tribunal for war crimes against Moslems, said they would prove incompetence of the prosecution's expert witnesses.

- Dorica Nikolic, a member of the opposition Social Liberal paty (HSLS) who held talks with the ruling HDZ on power sharing in the capital without the consent of the party leadership, refused to step down from her position of head of the Zagreb HSLS branch.

- Bank of Austria granted food concern Podravka 20 million German marks for its financial restructuring and investment. The loan is a five-year facility with the one-year grace period and the interest rate of little over four percent.

- Hot but short tourist summer -- tourists are coming back to the Adriatic, but mostly in July and August. The capacities utilisation in the two key months reached 80 percent of the 1990 level, one year before the war broke out scaring tourists away.

- Vladimir Primorac, a distinguished member of the Social Liberal party (SLP), says "neither (Drazen) Budisa not (Vladimir) Gotovac, but someone else" (should lead the party). The two top SLP officials are fighting for power and Primorac said the crisis has reached its peak.
- British pop star David Bowie performs in Zagreb on July 1, for the first time since 1990.
- Croatia reappeared on the road map of Europe, report from Helsinki.

- Restauration company "Vicko Andric" won this year's conservation award for rebuilding the cupola of the Sibenik dome, the 16-century marble masterpiece built by Master Radovan, which suffered heavy damages in a Serb artillery bombardment in 1991.

- Croatian public company, Croatian Forestry, took over control of forests in the last Serb-held enclave of Eastern Slavonia. These include over 50,000 hectars of forests and six forestries. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
